criterion: Across the film on the home page, tone is drawn as engraved parallel hatching that stays fixed to each surface as the camera moves.
evaluation_rule: The film is the full-window rendered story on the home page. Hatching means shading made of parallel engraved lines rather than smooth gradients. Yes if figures, columns and sky are shaded with such lines that travel with their surface, faces keep more in-between tone than stone, columns deep in the colonnade still read as separate lines, every small mark such as the standing-figure ornament, the arrows and the panel frames is drawn rather than loaded as a picture, and each frame leads with its subject. No if any surface is smoothly shaded, the lines slide across the screen like a filter, distant columns clog into black, or a mark arrives as an image file.

criterion: The palette of the film holds ink black, warm paper, bone white and one saturated red, with the three flavour tints as the only strong accents.
evaluation_rule: Allowed colours are near-black ink and its dark greys, warm off-white paper, pure white bone, the saturated temple red and its darker relatives, the muted orange and warm greys of the robe and stone, and the flavour tints: light cyan for Marshmallow Coffee, light green for Mint Chocolate and pale yellow-amber for Orange Chocolate. Answer yes when every frame keeps to that set and each tint appears only with its flavour. Answer no when another hue family, such as purple, bright blue or a neon, shows up, or a tint decorates something that is not its flavour.

criterion: The temple chapters of the film show two rows of red columns, engraved eyes on the far wall, breathing light beams and an altar holding three bottles.
evaluation_rule: The temple chapters run from the portal through the collapse after the pour; the robe there is a light muted orange until a flavour is chosen. Beams breathe when their brightness shifts slowly without a visible loop, and the portal and the breaking columns move in visible jerks, as hand-drawn animation does, while robe, floating rocks and beams all lean with one wind. A yes needs all of this on screen, the robe colour included, while driving through those chapters. A no follows when an element is missing, the robe is another colour, the beams are a static glow, the portal or fracture glides smoothly, or things blow in different directions.

criterion: Changing flavour in the product carousel slides the flavour names sideways as the bottle stays centred and refills in the new tint.
evaluation_rule: The product carousel is the collection chapter showing one bottle over its outlined flavour name, with next, previous and side-label controls; from the promise chapter on, words hold still for reading. Yes if pressing next moves the names across while the bottle holds its place and its liquid changes colour, and the tasting notes read without moving. No if the bottle slides away with the names, the liquid keeps the old colour, or the words drift while being read.

criterion: In the film on the home page, comic panels of the outdoor chapters have hand-drawn wobbly frames with narration boxes pinned to their corners.
evaluation_rule: A narration box is the white, ink-bordered box of capitals telling the story. Panel frames are four separate, slightly uneven strokes whose ink thickness stays the same as panels grow, with square corners. Say yes when the frames look like that and each narration box sits at a panel corner, where it may overhang. Say no when frames are clean or rounded rectangles, fatten as panels scale, or boxes are centred on their panels.

criterion: The story of the film stops advancing the moment a slow scroll stops, and chapter changes blend rather than cut.
evaluation_rule: The film is driven by the wheel, a trackpad, touch or keys. A flick may coast briefly; idle breathing of figures, the pulsing gate prompt and the breathing beams may continue on their own. Yes if releasing a slow held scroll stops the story advancing within a frame and every chapter change is a cross-blend. No if the story keeps advancing after a slow scroll stops, or a chapter change cuts or pops in.

criterion: The where page shows the venue list beside a plan drawn in the film's engraved line work, with venues holding the selected flavour marked in red.
evaluation_rule: The where page is the venue finder; each venue on its plan is marked by the small standing-figure ornament, and the flavour is chosen with a picker on the page. Yes if a hatched plan sits beside the list, marks use the ornament, and venues with the chosen flavour turn red when the picker changes. No if the list stands alone, marks are generic pins, or no venue changes colour with the picker.

criterion: The still page shows a still picture of each chapter's composition in story order.
evaluation_rule: The still page is the ordinary document reached at the home address with mode set to still. A yes needs one picture per chapter, eighteen in all, each recognisably the chapter's composition, readable without driving anything. A no follows when pictures are missing, generic, or out of story order.

criterion: On the cellar shelf of visitor2, the expired Nocturne N.01 bottle carries the went-back line and shows the absence of any countdown.
evaluation_rule: The cellar shelf is the signed-in page of kept bottles; sign in as visitor2@example.com with deku-demo-pw-2026. The went-back line is IT WENT BACK. CLAIM ANOTHER, compared ignoring letter case and surrounding space. Countdowns belong only to holds with under six hours left. Yes if the N01 bottle shows that line and neither that bottle nor the confirmed N02 bottle shows a countdown. No if the line is missing or reworded, or any bottle there shows a countdown.

criterion: The audio meter in the lower right corner of the film dances with the sound once switched on.
evaluation_rule: The audio meter is the four-bar control named Toggle audio. A yes needs silence before the meter is first pressed, then bars moving with the live mix; at rest the meter is a still two-bar mark. A no follows when any sound plays before the press, the bars stay still while sound plays, or the resting mark is missing.

criterion: With the connection cut, the shelf and the venue list keep their last content marked as possibly stale, and the tastings page and ritual builder explain why an action waits.
evaluation_rule: Cutting the connection means going offline in the browser after the pages loaded once; the film keeps playing from the story it already has. Yes if the shelf and venue list still render with a staleness mark, the tastings page shows existing bookings and refuses new holds in a sentence, the builder refuses saving in a sentence, and the film still plays. No if any surface spins forever, goes blank, or fails silently.

criterion: The tastings booking form keeps the chosen session and party size when a seat hold lapses or the sign-in expires mid-booking.
evaluation_rule: The booking form is the step sequence on the tastings page, which is choose a session, set a party size, hold seats, give a name, then confirm. A lapsed hold is one past its fifteen minutes; an expired sign-in is a session token that has run out. Answer yes when each event brings the visitor back, after signing in again if needed, to the party size step with the session and size still chosen and a sentence saying why. Answer no when the visitor lands at the start with choices cleared, or gets no explanation.

criterion: Refusals and empty lists across the additions name what failed, why and the one next action.
evaluation_rule: The additions are the cellar shelf, the where page, the tastings page and the ritual builder. A good refusal says what went wrong, why and what to do next; invalid form fields are named inline and keep what was typed; each empty list reads differently from its loading state and says what would fill it. Yes when every refusal and empty list met on those pages behaves that way. No when a message only says something went wrong, a field loses its text, or an empty list is a blank area.

criterion: The header pill word for the current chapter sits at full strength, and the four named primary actions each carry the strongest contrast on their surface.
evaluation_rule: The header pill is the rounded bar at the top right: EXPERIENCE is current from the first chapter through the temple collapse, COLLECTION from the colonnade on. The primary actions are KEEP THIS ONE beneath the carousel data strip, TELL ME WHEN IT LANDS on an empty venue list, the hold and confirm steps of a tasting, and NAME IT in the ritual builder. Yes if the current word is darker than the other and each named action is the most prominent control where it appears. No if both words look alike, or another control outshines a named action.

criterion: The cookie question appears once, after the age panel closes, as a small notice at the lower left of the film.
evaluation_rule: The cookie question asks about remembering the sound preference and a ritual draft. A first visit should show the notice only after the age answer, at the lower left clear of the audio meter, and a reload after answering should not show the notice again. Yes when all three hold. No when the notice sits anywhere other than the lower left, covers the middle of the film, comes before the age panel, or returns after an answer.

criterion: The product bottle and the coupe glass look photographic, lit with reflections, inside an otherwise engraved film.
evaluation_rule: The bottle appears in the product carousel and the glass in the pour and poster chapters. A yes needs glossy highlights on both, a printed paper-grained label wrapped around the bottle, and hatching everywhere else. A no follows when the bottle or glass is hatched like the rest, the label is a flat sticker, or other objects are also realistic.

criterion: In the collection act, the poster chapter sets a solid block of display capitals with the coupe glass over the centre, the lettering visibly bent through the liquid.
evaluation_rule: The poster chapter follows the promise chapter, whose one light paragraph sits justified at about a third of the frame width. Yes if the promise paragraph looks like that, set in a light long-form face, and the poster type touches line to line behind the glass with the letters seen through the liquid distorted. No if the paragraph is ragged or full width, the glass sits in a cut-out gap, or the type behind it is undistorted.

criterion: The cellar shelf shows kept bottles standing on an engraved stone ledge, each turning slowly, entering like the header bar unrolls.
evaluation_rule: The shelf belongs to the signed-in cellar page, and a visitor with zero, one or three bottles all see a sensible arrangement there. Yes if bottles stand on a hatched ledge, turn gently out of step, show their state as a word, and the shelf arrives with a long settling entrance. No if bottles appear as a grid of cards or flat thumbnails, stand still, arrive with no entrance, or show states by colour only.

criterion: Headlines on the home page use a tall, high-contrast serif in capitals, with labels in a heavy rounded sans in spaced capitals.
evaluation_rule: Headlines are the chapter titles, flavour names and the title lockup, and the lockup's middle line is the largest type anywhere in the product. Yes if those use a sharp serif with hairline strokes, the header words, narration and data strip use a heavy rounded sans, and nothing is larger than the lockup. No if headlines are set in a sans or another non-serif face, a single generic sans carries everything, or other type outsizes the lockup.

criterion: The ritual builder sits on a red ground with paper-coloured type, and the other additions share the film's ink, paper and red.
evaluation_rule: The other additions are the cellar shelf, the where page and the tastings page; their gaps line up on one repeating spacing step. Yes if the builder's background is the saturated red with off-white text, the other three use paper grounds, ink type, red accents and evenly stepped spacing, figures in lists line up in columns, and the product offers no separate light or dark mode. No if any addition uses a stock theme in other colours, spacing looks arbitrary, figures wobble out of column, or a light or dark mode switch exists.

criterion: The furniture of the film moves with eased character, and the finished ritual card lands with the product's one overshoot.
evaluation_rule: Furniture means the age panel, the header pill and the venue plan marks. Expected moments are hovering Yes or No on the age panel turning its frame and word red almost at once, the panel splitting into shutters that tip away while its buttons trail, the header background unrolling after the loader and its words rising a beat apart left to right, venue marks arriving nearest first, opening a venue moving the plan in on it without changing page, and the ritual card settling past its place. Yes when those moments appear with smooth easing. No when any appears abruptly or all at once, hover shows no red change, the panel dissolves flat, the page changes on opening a venue, or something else overshoots.

criterion: Keyboard, reduced-motion and contrast needs are met across the film and the additions.
evaluation_rule: Checks: tabbing reaches the audio control, the age panel buttons, both held gates and the controls named previous slide, next slide, left text and right text with a visible ring; focus stays inside the open age panel; with reduced motion requested the film steps between still frames and each gate takes one press; switching the whole frame between black, red and paper never flashes; focus returns to the page when the age panel closes; the drawing surface never takes focus; no text a visitor must read is smaller than the base text; text meets WCAG AA contrast; targets are comfortably sized; images carry alternative text; meaning never rests on colour alone. Yes when all of these hold. No when any fails.

criterion: The film keeps each shot's full height at every width, and the additions reflow into a stacked layout at a narrow viewport.
evaluation_rule: A narrow viewport is an upright handset width; the additions are the cellar, where, tastings and ritual pages. Yes if narrowing the window crops or extends only the sides of film shots, a sideways handset shows round arrows beside the carousel bottle, and the additions stack their parts with every control reachable and no sideways scrolling. No if a shot crops at top or bottom, or an addition spills past the edge.

criterion: The venue plan beside the venues list loads map tiles or scripts from an outside mapping service.
evaluation_rule: An outside mapping service is any third-party map provider, its tiles or its script. Yes if the plan shows such a map or the page requests one. No if the plan is drawn entirely by the product itself.

criterion: A soft blurred drop shadow sits under a figure in the film.
evaluation_rule: Figures are the hooded Saint and the reaching hand. Yes if a smooth, blurred shadow appears beneath any of them. No if every shadow under a figure is hatched or stippled like the rest of the engraving.
